claims.claim: Adding body-turn words to the complete compass route improves the prospective reviewer’s endpoint accuracy.
The relative command string FRFF reaches the same endpoint from every cardinal initial heading at the same start.
Map-right and body-right always denote the same compass direction.
Coordinates can replace orientation in every checkpoint for a relative walk.
The number of forward moves and right turns determines a relative path endpoint, regardless of order.
Replacing R by L preserves the endpoint of every route with one quarter-turn.
A qualitative distance word such as nearby fixes an exact endpoint on the declared integer grid.
A list of compass bearings determines an endpoint without leg lengths.
A printed legend makes the route decodable in a spoken excerpt that omits the legend.
Every compass-only route needs the walker’s initial body heading to determine its endpoint.
Two conflicting direction descriptions still specify one executable move without a precedence rule.
Interchanging the x and y axes leaves every coordinate route unchanged.
Repeating a route’s forward commands from its endpoint necessarily returns to its start.
An unlabeled arrow uniquely identifies entrance orientation in every diagram.
A path index alone determines the next relative move across all route instances.
The shortest wording always leaves the fewest unresolved route values.
A destination name alone determines coordinates even when its location map is absent.
A correct endpoint guarantees the route obeyed every intermediate restriction.

findings.text: The same-position countercase leaves the next relative F displacement underdetermined by position alone.
A sufficient relative-walk checkpoint includes orientation as well as position.
With that pair, each F token selects exactly one of four cardinal displacement vectors.
A turn token updates orientation modulo four before later displacement lookup.
Consequently the same multiset of tokens can select different displacement sequences when order changes.
The stronger candidate that endpoint depends only on token counts fails on FRF versus RFF.
A checkpoint plus an ordered suffix determines the remaining walk under the declared deterministic decoder.
At held-out start (2,3), east-facing FRFF ends (3,1), while north-facing FRFF ends (4,4).
